54043-the-life-of-cardinal-wolsey.creator: Unknown

arxiv-2103-02293.title: Room Temperature Light-Mediated Long-Range Coupling of Excitons in Perovskites
arxiv-2103-02293.creator: Tanjung Krisnanda, Qiannan Zhang, Kevin Dini, David Giovanni, Timothy C. H. Liew, Tze Chien Sum
arxiv-2103-02293.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Tanjung Krisnanda, Qiannan Zhang, Kevin Dini, David Giovanni, Timothy C. H. Liew, Tze Chien Sum. Perovskites have been the focus of attention due to their multitude of outstanding optoelectronic properties and structural versatility. Two-dimensional halide perovskite such as ( C 6 ​ H 5 ​ C 2 ​ H 4 ​ N H 3 ) 2 ​ Pb I 4 (\mbox{C}_{6}\mbox{H}_{5}\mbox{C}_{2}\mbox{H}_{4}\mbox{N}\mbox{H}_{3})_{2}\mbox{Pb}\mbox{I}_{4} , or simply PEPI, forms natural multiple quantum wells with enhanced light-matter interactions, making them attractive systems for further investigation.

arxiv-2103-05627.title: Survival functions versus conditional aggregation-based survival functions on discrete space Journal: Information Sciences
arxiv-2103-05627.creator: Basarik Stanislav, Borzová Jana, Halčinová Lenka
arxiv-2103-05627.description: Abstract In this paper we deal with conditional aggregation-based survival functions recently introduced by Boczek et al. (2020). The concept is worth to study because of its possible implementation in real-life situations and mathematical theory as well. The aim of this paper is the comparison of this new notion with the standard survival function.

arxiv-2203-01022.title: Suppression of the TeV pair-beam plasma instability by a tangled weak intergalactic magnetic field Journal: AAS The Astrophysical Journal
arxiv-2203-01022.creator: Mahmoud Alawashra, Martin Pohl
arxiv-2203-01022.description: Abstract We study the effect of a tangled sub-fG level intergalactic magnetic field (IGMF) on the electrostatic instability of a blazar-induced pair beam. Sufficiently strong IGMF may significantly deflect the TeV pair beams, which would reduce the flux of secondary cascade emission below the observational limits.

arxiv-2304-07592.title: Leveraging Composition-Based Material Descriptors for Machine Learning Optimization
arxiv-2304-07592.creator: Giovanni Trezza, Eliodoro Chiavazzo
arxiv-2304-07592.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Giovanni Trezza, Eliodoro Chiavazzo. In this study, we evaluate several classifiers and focus on selecting a minimal set of appropriate material features. Our objective is to propose and discuss general strategies for reducing the number of descriptors required for material classification. The first strategy involves testing whether the critical temperature of the target material property is invariant with respect to binary groups of composition-based features. We also propose a multi-objective optimization procedure to reduce the set of composition-based material descriptors.

arxiv-2304-13452.title: On signed Mordell-Weil groups for abelian varieties.
arxiv-2304-13452.creator: Jishnu Ray
arxiv-2304-13452.description: Abstract . In this short note, we work in the general framework of supersingular abelian varieties defined over ℚ \mathbb{Q} . Using Coleman maps constructed by Büyükboduk–Lei, we define some new objects called “the multi-signed Mordell-Weil groups" for supersingular abelian varieties, provide an explicit structure of the dual of these groups as an Iwasawa module and prove a control theorem.

arxiv-2507-02565.title: Reconstructing Close Human Interaction with Appearance and Proxemics Reasoning
arxiv-2507-02565.creator: Buzhen Huang Chen Li Chongyang Xu Dongyue Lu Jinnan Chen, Yangang Wang Gim Hee Lee
arxiv-2507-02565.description: Abstract Due to visual ambiguities and inter-person occlusions, existing human pose estimation methods cannot recover plausible close interactions from in-the-wild videos. Even state-of-the-art large foundation models ( e.g . , SAM) cannot accurately distinguish human semantics in such challenging scenarios. In this work, we find that human appearance can provide a straightforward cue to address these obstacles.

arxiv-2508-00520.title: An Observed Evidence for the Primordial Origin of Galaxy Sizes
arxiv-2508-00520.creator: Jun-Sung Moon 1,2,3 and Jounghun Lee 1
arxiv-2508-00520.description: Abstract We present an observational evidence supporting the scenario that the protogalactic angular momenta play the most decisive role in molding the optical sizes of present galaxies. Analyzing the NASA-Sloan Atlas catalog in the redshift range of 0.02 ≤ z < 0.09 0.02\leq z<0.

arxiv-2509-16827.title: Inverse-Designed Photonic Crystal Cavities with Controllable Far-Field Numerical Aperture
arxiv-2509-16827.creator: Neelesh Kumar Vij, Purbita Purkayastha, Jasvith Raj Basani, Edo Waks
arxiv-2509-16827.description: Abstract Photonic crystal cavities confine light to subwavelength volumes, enabling strong light-matter interactions for applications in low-power photonics, opto-electronics, nonlinear optics, and quantum information. These applications demand cavities that combine high quality factors, low mode volumes, and high coupling efficiencies. However, optimizing across these metrics requires exploring a large design space, motivating the use of inverse design strategies.

arxiv-2509-24480.title: Magnus submonoids and membership problems in one-relator, surface and hyperbolic groups Thanks: The research of the authors was supported by the EPSRC Fellowship grant EP/V032003/1 ‘Algorithmic, topological and geometric aspects of infinite groups, monoids and inverse semigroups’.
arxiv-2509-24480.description: Abstract . Motivated by its applications to the word problem for one-relator inverse monoids, via results of Ivanov, Margolis, and Meakin (2001), we prove several decidability and undecidability results about the submonoid membership problem in one-relator, surface and hyperbolic groups. The membership problem in free-by-cyclic one-relator groups is undecidable in general.

arxiv-2601-18462.title: Rethinking AI in the age of climate collapse: Ethics, power, and responsibility
arxiv-2601-18462.creator: Julio Vega
arxiv-2601-18462.description: Abstract Abstract The climate crisis requires responses that integrate scientific, ethical, social, and technological perspectives. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a powerful tool in climate modelling, environmental monitoring, and energy optimisation, yet its growing use also raises critical environmental, ethical, legal, and social questions.

openalex-w1979808851.title: High Malnutrition Rate in Venezuelan Yanomami Compared to Warao Amerindians and Creoles: Significant Associations WITH Intestinal Parasites and Anemia
openalex-w1979808851.creator: Lilly M. Verhagen, Renzo Nino Incani, Carolina R. Franco, Alejandra Ugarte, Yeneska Cadenas, Carmen I. Sierra Ruiz, Peter W. M. Hermans, Denise Hoek, Maiza Campos Ponce, Jacobus Henri de Waard, Elena Pinelli
openalex-w1979808851.description: BACKGROUND: Children in rural areas experience the interrelated problems of poor growth, anemia and parasitic infections. We investigated the prevalence of and associations between intestinal helminth and protozoan infections, malnutrition and anemia in school-age Venezuelan...

plos-pone-0005368.title: Comparative Proteomics Analyses Reveal the vir B of B. melitensis Affects Expression of Intracellular Survival Related Proteins
plos-pone-0005368.creator: Yufei Wang, Zeliang Chen, Feng Qiao et al.
plos-pone-0005368.description: PLOS ONE research article. Brucella melitensis is a facultative, intracellular, pathogenic bacterium that replicates within macrophages. The type IV secretion system encoded by the virB operon ( virB ) is involved in Brucella intracellular survival. However, the underlying molecular mechanisms, especially

pmc-10543325.title: Comparing exercise determinants between Black and White older adults with heart failure
pmc-10543325.creator: Navin Kaushal, Donya Nemati, Dylan Mann-Krzisnik, Adrián Noriega de la Colina
pmc-10543325.description: BackgroundHeart Failure is a leading cause of mortality among older adults. Engaging in regular exercise at moderate-to-vigorous intensity has been shown to improve survival rates. Theory-informed methodologies have been recommended to promote exercise, but limited application of theoretical framework has been conducted for understanding racial disparities among older adults with heart failure.

pmc-10648035.title: Endo-Periodontal Lesions—An Overlooked Etiology of Odontogenic Sinusitis
pmc-10648035.creator: Jianyou Wu, Ming Zheng, Xiangdong Wang, Songlin Wang, Carlos Marcelo Da Silva Figueredo, Marco Tatullo
pmc-10648035.description: The aim of this study was to analyze the oral etiology of patients with odontogenic sinusitis (ODS) and to compare the differences in demographic data, clinical symptoms, extent of sinus involvement, bone penetration of the maxillary sinus floor (MSF) between different etiologies. A retrospective investigation was conducted on 103 patients with ODS recruited from Beijing TongRen Hospital.

pmc-11491179.title: Embracing industry in the development of robotic coronary bypass grafting—the sun rises in the East
pmc-11491179.creator: Senne De Groote, Nora Marain, Gianluca Torregrossa, Wouter Oosterlinck
pmc-11491179.description: The introduction of robotic surgical devices nearly two decades ago led to a significant reduction in the invasiveness of cardiac procedures. The further worldwide implementation of robotic surgical devices in cardiac surgery, especially coronary artery bypass grafting and mitral valve repair or replacement, has, however, been stalled by numerous challenges.

pmc-11662405.title: Visualization of residual gaps after linear ablation using the LUMIPOINTTM module: A case report
pmc-11662405.creator: Yasuyuki Egami, Yasuharu Matsunaga-Lee, Masamichi Yano, Masami Nishino
pmc-11662405.description: BackgroundMacroreentrant atrial tachycardia (ATs) through epicardial conduction is depicted as a focal AT on 3-D mapping, i.e., pseudo-focal AT. A new feature of the Rhythmia mapping system (Boston Scientific), the "LUMIPOINT module", can highlight all electrocardiograms (EGMs) above a threshold determined by an adjustable confidence slider (CS).

pmc-11713055.title: Measuring What Matters Most to People Living with Alzheimer’s Disease and Care Partners: What Matters Most Quantitative Research Development
pmc-11713055.creator: Carla (DeMuro) Romano, Emily Bratlee‐Whitaker, Ann Hartry, Elizabeth S Mearns, Jim Taylor, Geri Taylor, Leigh F Callahan, Doreen Monks, Ian Kremer, Debra Lappin, Theresa Frangiosa, Sanjyot Sangodkar, William L Herring, Kajan Gnanasakthy, Diana Goss, Lori McLeod, Teresa Edwards, Christie Poulos, Dana
pmc-11713055.description: BackgroundPrevious What Matters Most (WMM) research identified and verified patient‐important concepts among a diverse population of people living with Alzheimer’s disease (PLWAD) and their care partners across all stages of Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Additionally, a conceptual model of disease was developed using hypothesized domains and was further refined using qualitative data (Figure 1).

pmc-12486491.title: Changes in primary health care service experiences and urban–suburban disparities among Shanghai residents: a two-year comparative study
pmc-12486491.creator: Yang Sen, Li Wanyu, Shi Jianwei, Shi Leiyu, Ma Le, Pan Ying, Wang Yang, Gu Chao, Zhang Hanzhi, Guo Mengruo, Jin Hua, Yu Dehua
pmc-12486491.description: BackgroundPrimary health care (PHC) is central to achieving universal health coverage, yet longitudinal assessments of residents’ experiences—especially regarding urban–suburban disparities—remain scarce. This study aims to examine changes in PHC service experiences among Shanghai residents between 2023 and 2024, identify urban–suburban differences, and explore key influencing factors.

pmc-12739867.title: Real-world outcomes in patients with relapsed and refractory multiple myeloma with prior proteasome inhibitor and lenalidomide exposure: A single-center study in Sweden
pmc-12739867.creator: Vincent Luong, Muhammad Kashif, Katarina Uttervall, Anna Bohlin, Annette Öster Fernström, Ying Qu, Seina Lee, João Mendes, Sandra Van Hoorenbeeck, Eva Hellqvist Franck, Jianming He, Evren Alici, Johan Lund
pmc-12739867.description: The use of proteasome inhibitors (PI) and immunomodulatory drugs (IMiD) such as lenalidomide (Len) in early lines of therapy in multiple myeloma (MM) has resulted in a high proportion of patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM) being Len-refractory. Len refractoriness is associated with inferior outcomes, constituting an unmet need in clinical practice.

pmc-12858153.title: Interplay of pilgrimage, cultural tourism, and psychological well-being: An institutional experience of running sub-center hospital in Mahakumbh 2025 Prayagraj
pmc-12858153.creator: Shruti Sinha, Purushottam Kumar, Suyash Singh, Abhay Singh, Rajat S. Das
pmc-12858153.description: Background:This study explores the psychological and physiological dimensions of religious pilgrimage participation among attendees of Mahakumbh 2025, focusing on individuals seeking care at a psychiatry outpatient department.Methodology:We examined the relationships between demographic factors (age, gender), frequency of pilgrimage participation, body mass index (BMI), cognitive functioning (as measured by MOCA), and depressive symptoms (HAM-D).

pmc-13417265.title: Light/NADH Bistimulation ATP Synthesis Artificial Organelles for Nitrogen Assimilation and RNA Transcription in Artificial Cells
pmc-13417265.creator: Yongshuo Ren, Weichen Wang, Jingjing Zhao, Yan Zhao, Yingming Zhao, Shubin Li, Yanhao Liu, Xiaojun Han
pmc-13417265.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Energy supply is a fundamental requirement for maintaining a complex metabolic network within the artificial cells. RNA transcription is a key step in the genetic inheritance of artificial cells. Targeting these two key issues in the field of artificial cells, a light/NADH bisimulation adenosine triphosphate (ATP) synthesis artificial organelle (LNAO) capable of producing ATP through two distinct pathways is built to power reactions within artificial cells.

pmc-13446159.title: Heterostructured Materials for Room‐Temperature Na‐S Batteries: Directional Design Strategies and Multifaceted Applications
pmc-13446159.creator: Yeqing Yang, Xue Li, Kunjie Zhu, Xiang‐Long Huang, Yun‐Xiao Wang
pmc-13446159.description: The development of room‐temperature sodium‐sulfur (RT Na‐S) batteries is fundamentally constrained by many severe challenges, including the polysulfide shuttle effect, sluggish sulfur conversion kinetics, and unstable sodium metal anode. This comprehensive review systematically presents a universal and versatile materials design methodology, heterostructure engineering, to concurrently address these interlinked challenges.

pmc-13685174.title: The Analgesic Efficacy of Adding Dexmedetomidine to Ropivacaine in Preoperative Interscalene Block for Arthroscopic Rotator Cuff Repair
pmc-13685174.creator: Mahmood-Reza Alebouyeh, Saeed Reza Entezary, Shirin Zarandooz, Masood Mohseni
pmc-13685174.description: BackgroundEffective postoperative pain management is essential after arthroscopic shoulder surgery. Ultrasound-guided interscalene block (ISB) is widely used for perioperative analgesia; however, the benefits of adding dexmedetomidine to local anesthetics remain uncertain.ObjectivesThis study aimed to evaluate the analgesic efficacy and hemodynamic effects of dexmedetomidine as an adjuvant to ropivacaine for ultrasound-guided ISB in patients undergoing arthroscopic rotator cuff repair.
